svg.text: Why Walker-Vose Alias Tables Eliminate the Transcendental Rotation Bottleneck (Grover-Rudolph [2002]):

text.font-family: 'Latin Modern Roman', 'CMU Serif', 'STIX Two Text', 'Times New Roman', Georgia, serif

svg.text: • Grover-Rudolph Binary-Tree State Prep: Requires w = 8 sequential stages of multiplexed controlled-R_y(theta_k) rotations,

text.font-family: 'Latin Modern Roman', 'CMU Serif', 'STIX Two Text', 'Times New Roman', Georgia, serif

svg.text: where each arbitrary angle theta_k = 2*arccos(sqrt(P_L / P_parent)) must be synthesized via Ross-Selinger grids (~50 T-gates * 8 = ~400+ T-gates).

text.font-family: 'Latin Modern Roman', 'CMU Serif', 'STIX Two Text', 'Times New Roman', Georgia, serif

svg.text: • Walker-Vose O(1)-Comparison Alias Method: Classical O(2^w) Robin-Hood preprocessing pairs each sub-average outcome i

text.font-family: 'Latin Modern Mono', 'CMU Typewriter Text', 'JetBrains Mono', 'Courier New', monospace

svg.text: with a super-average donor Alias[i]. On the quantum computer, ONLY Clifford+Toffoli integer operations are executed:

text.font-family: 'Latin Modern Roman', 'CMU Serif', 'STIX Two Text', 'Times New Roman', Georgia, serif

svg.text: Qubits: 2*w + 2*mu + 1 = 49 Q | Toffolis: 2^w (QROAM) + mu (Cmp) + w (CSWAP) = 256 + 16 + 8 = 280 CCX | Arbitrary R_y Gates: ZERO!
